# Device speed in history feature (2026-02-06 16:47Z)

_**User**_

there has been a new feature added that displays a devices current speed in the "updated"-text of the map marker when the speed is >10km/h.

I want to add this functionality to the history feature as well. Would that work and can each point of history therefore show the date, time (as it is now) and the speed if available?

        "contents": ") -&gt; String {\n    guard let date = date else { return \"–\" }\n    let diff = now.timeIntervalSince(date)\n    if date &gt; now {\n        return NSLocalizedString(\"relative_time_now\", comment: \"Indicates that the location update just happened or is happening right now in a relative time on the map marker.\")\n    } else if diff &lt; timeConsideredNow {\n        return NSLocalizedString(\"relative_time_now\", comment: \"Indicates that the location update just happened or is happening right now in a relative time on the map marker.\")\n    }\n    let formatter = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()\n    formatter.unitsStyle = unitsStyle\n    return formatter.localizedString(for: date, relativeTo: now)\n}\n\n/// Returns a formatted speed string for map labels when speed exceeds 10 km/h.\nfunc mapSpeedLabelText(speedMetersPerSecond: Double?) -&gt; String? Color.black.opacity(0.6) : Color.white.opacity(0.7))\n                    .lineLimit(1)\n                    .truncationMode(.tail)\n                    .contentTransition(.identity)\n                    .animation(nil, value: subtitle)\n                // Placemark (always render)\n                let place = placemarkText(from: displayedCachedLocation)\n                Text(place)\n                    .font(.caption)\n                    .foregroundColor(colorScheme == .light ? 0.7 : 0.4))\n        )\n    }\n\n    private func overlayMetrics(for family: WidgetFamily) -&gt; (Font, Font, CGFloat, CGFloat) {\n        switch family {\n        case .systemMedium:\n            return (.subheadline.weight(.semibold), .caption2, 2, 7)\n        case .systemLarge:\n            return (.headline, .subheadline, 3, 12)\n        default:\n            return (.subheadline.weight(.semibold), .caption, 2, 8)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private var overlayWidthFactor: CGFloat {\n        switch family {\n        case .systemMedium: return 0.9\n        case .systemLarge: return 0.92\n        default: return 0.9\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func formattedLocality(for device: WidgetDeviceData) -&gt; String {\n        let locality = device.locality ??         "contents": "    private func focusOnScrubbedEntry(animated: Bool = true) {\n        guard let scrubTimestamp else { return }\n        guard let target = viewModel.closest(to: scrubTimestamp, in: selectedRange) else { return }\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            updateRegion(animated: animated, using: [target], useDefaultZoom: true)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func color(for entry: MiataruLocationData, within entries: [MiataruLocationData]) -&gt; Color {\n        // Use the full history to keep a consistent color mapping regardless of timeline selection\n        let reference = viewModel.history.isEmpty ? Summary of what’s in place:

**Yes, it works.** History uses the same `MiataruLocationData` type as the live map. That type already has an optional `Speed` (in m/s), and the server can store it per location, so history points can show speed when it was recorded.

**What was implemented**

- **Where:** The history map’s selected-marker label in `iPhone_DeviceHistoryMapView` (the text above the pin when you select a history point).
- **Logic:** Reused the same helper as the live map: `mapSpeedLabelText(speedMetersPerSecond:)` from `MapHelpers.swift`. So:
  - Speed is shown only when it’s **> 10 km/h** (same rule as the “updated” text on the live map).
  - Format is locale-aware (e.g. `45 km/h` or `28 mph`).
- **Label content:** Each selected history point now shows:
  - **Date and time** (unchanged, from `timelineDateFormatter`, e.g. “2/6/25, 3:45 PM”).
